name: GitHub MCP Server
author: GitHub
description: GitHub's official MCP server for repos, issues, PRs, Actions, code scanning and more, available as a remote server or a Docker image. It is the standard way to give an agent GitHub access. Use the hosted endpoint with OAuth, or run the container with a fine-grained token.
use_case: Ask your agent to triage this week's open issues, label them and draft a fix PR for the top bug without leaving the chat.
safety_notes: Official; use a fine-grained token with least privilege
works_with: Claude Code; Codex; Cursor; OpenCode; Gemini CLI; Grok Bot / any MCP client
install: Remote: https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/ or docker run -i --rm -e GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN ghcr.io/github/github-mcp-server

name: Codex CLI
author: OpenAI
description: Codex CLI is OpenAI's open-source coding agent that runs locally, reads and edits your repo and runs commands inside an OS sandbox with approval modes; it also has IDE and desktop front ends and supports skills, plugins and MCP. A primary coding agent option. Install with `npm i -g @openai/codex` or the official install script.
use_case: Point Codex at a failing test suite in your repo and let it fix the failures inside its sandbox, approving each command before it touches the network.
safety_notes: Official; sandboxed by default; installer is OpenAI's own script. Defaults: workspace-write sandbox with network off and on-request approvals; `exec` is read-only; --yolo removes sandbox and prompts. OTel export off by default.
accounts_needed: ChatGPT plan or OpenAI API key

name: agent-browser
author: Vercel Labs
description: A native Rust CLI for browser automation by agents: `snapshot` returns the page as compact text with refs like @e1, the agent acts on a ref, then re-reads the page. The browser stays open between commands, so each step is one cheap shell call, and it can also run as an MCP server. Install with `npm install -g agent-browser` then `agent-browser install` to fetch Chrome for Testing.
use_case: Let a coding agent click through your web app's checkout flow step by step with compact page snapshots, keeping token cost low on long sessions.
safety_notes: Official Vercel Labs; ships trust-boundary docs telling agents page text is untrusted; postinstall only fetches its own binary
works_with: Claude Code; Codex; Cursor; OpenCode; Gemini CLI; Grok Bot / any MCP client

name: Context7
author: Upstash
description: Context7 feeds coding agents current, version-specific library docs and examples so they stop using stale or invented APIs. You add 'use context7' to a prompt or let the agent call it. Set up with `npx ctx7 setup`, which configures the MCP server or skill for your agent.
use_case: Building against a library that shipped a breaking release last month, add "use context7" so the agent writes code from the current docs instead of a stale API.
safety_notes: Well-known; sends your library queries to Upstash
works_with: Claude Code; Codex; Cursor; OpenCode; Gemini CLI; Grok Bot / any MCP client
accounts_needed: Optional Context7 API key for higher limits

name: Playwright MCP
author: Microsoft
description: Microsoft's MCP server that lets an agent drive a real browser through Playwright using accessibility snapshots instead of screenshots. Good for testing web apps and automating sites from any MCP client. Add it with `claude mcp add playwright npx @playwright/mcp@latest` (similar one-liners for other clients).
use_case: After your agent changes a signup form, have it open the page, fill the form and confirm the success message actually appears.
safety_notes: Official; treat page content as untrusted input
works_with: Claude Code; Codex; Cursor; OpenCode; Gemini CLI; Grok Bot / any MCP client
ease_note: One-line add to any MCP client

name: promptfoo
author: Promptfoo
description: A CLI and library for evaluating and red-teaming LLM apps and agents: write test cases in YAML, compare prompts and models, run in CI, and generate attack suites. Now part of OpenAI and still MIT. Install with `npm install -g promptfoo` or `npx promptfoo@latest init`.
use_case: Before merging a prompt change, run a YAML test suite in CI that compares old and new prompts and fails the PR if accuracy drops or a jailbreak test passes.
safety_notes: Widely used; scan hits are documented attack examples
accounts_needed: Model API keys for the models you test

name: MCP Inspector
author: Model Context Protocol
description: The official MCP Inspector for testing MCP servers via a web UI, CLI or TUI: list tools, call them and watch messages. Essential when building your own servers. Run with `npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector`.
use_case: While building your own MCP server, open the Inspector to list its tools, call each one by hand and watch the raw JSON-RPC messages to debug a bad schema.
safety_notes: Official MCP project; keep it bound to localhost
works_with: Claude Code; Codex; Cursor; OpenCode; Gemini CLI; Grok Bot / any MCP client

name: Claude Agent SDK (Python)
author: Anthropic
description: A Python SDK that exposes the Claude Code agent loop (tools, hooks, subagents, sessions, permissions) so you can build your own agents on it. Install with `pip install claude-agent-sdk`; it drives the Claude Code CLI.
use_case: Build a custom PR-triage agent on the same loop Claude Code uses, with your own tools and permissions.
safety_notes: Official Anthropic; README suggests the Anthropic-hosted curl install script for the CLI
accounts_needed: Anthropic API key or Claude login

name: OpenHands
author: OpenHands
description: OpenHands (formerly OpenDevin) is now pitched as Agent Canvas: a self-hosted control center that runs OpenHands, Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Pi, OpenCode or any ACP agent across local, remote and cloud backends. You can start agent conversations, schedule automations such as decomposing GitHub issues into tasks, and post results to Slack. It fits a solo founder who wants an always-on agent team on their own hardware. Install with `npm install -g @openhands/agent-canvas` or run the Docker image.
use_case: Run Codex, Claude Code and OpenHands agents on different repos from one self-hosted control center and watch them side by side.
safety_notes: Well-known project; agents run in Docker sandboxes by default. Hits are its own installers and test fixtures. Point it at least-privilege tokens. Safety defaults not yet researched beyond the Docker sandbox.
ease_note: Docker or npm; more moving parts

name: Agent Skills (Addy Osmani)
author: Addy Osmani
description: Addy Osmani's production engineering skills that walk an agent through define, plan, build, verify, review and ship, with quality gates at each step. Aimed at teams who want senior-engineer habits enforced consistently. Install all 25 skills with `npx skills add addyosmani/agent-skills` or pick from the list.
use_case: Starting a new feature, have the agent walk define → plan → build → verify → review so it can't skip tests or ship without a review step.
safety_notes: Docs-first; skills explicitly tell agents to treat web content as data
works_with: Claude Code; Codex; Cursor; OpenCode; Gemini CLI

name: OpenCode
author: Anomaly (formerly SST)
description: OpenCode is an open-source coding agent with a polished TUI, desktop app and server mode, working with almost any model provider, with LSP integration, agents, skills and MCP. A popular alternative to Claude Code and Codex. Install with `npm i -g @opencode/cli@latest` or brew.
use_case: Run the same coding task against a local model and a cloud model from one TUI to compare cost and quality without switching tools.
safety_notes: Well-known team; installers are their own; hidden-Unicode hits are translations. `run --auto` approves everything not denied; `serve` can bind 0.0.0.0 and `pair --remote` exposes it to the internet. CLI telemetry default unknown.

name: Qwen Code
author: Qwen (Alibaba Cloud)
description: Qwen Code is Alibaba's open-source coding agent for the terminal, editors, desktop and chat, with auto-memory, skills, subagents, agent teams and MCP. It began as a fork of Google's Gemini CLI (v0.8.2) and has since diverged, and it speaks OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini and Qwen APIs or local models via Ollama/vLLM. It suits people who want a free, open model stack. Install with `npm install -g @qwen-code/qwen-code@latest` and run `qwen`.
use_case: Run a terminal coding agent tuned for Qwen models on a refactor, using subagents for tests and docs.
safety_notes: Official Alibaba Qwen org; prompt-injection hits are hostile-text test fixtures and a PR-safety checker; credential mentions are defensive docs
accounts_needed: Qwen OAuth or model API key
related_note: Fork of Gemini CLI v0.8.2, since diverged

name: Superpowers
author: Jesse Vincent (@obra)
description: A complete development methodology packaged as composable skills: brainstorm, plan, test-driven implementation, debugging and code review, with a bootstrap that makes the agent actually use them. It supports Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Pi and more. Install from the official Claude plugin directory or its own marketplace.
use_case: Before writing code for a new feature, have the agent brainstorm, write a plan, then implement test-first and request a code review of its own diff.
safety_notes: Docs-only skills; one SessionStart hook that only injects its own skill text
works_with: Claude Code; Codex; Cursor; OpenCode; Gemini CLI
ease_note: One-command plugin install on most agents

name: Crush
author: Charm
description: Crush is Charm's terminal coding agent. It works with many models (or any OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible API), lets you switch model mid-session, keeps several sessions per project, pulls extra context from language servers, and extends through MCP servers. It is for people who want a polished, model-agnostic TUI agent. Install with `brew install charmbracelet/tap/crush` or `npm install -g @charmland/crush`.
use_case: Switch from a fast cheap model to a stronger one mid-session in the terminal when a bug turns out to be harder than expected.
safety_notes: Official Charm repo; no risky patterns found. License is FSL-1.1-MIT (source-available, converts to MIT after two years), not OSI open source
ease_note: brew or npm, one config file

name: GitHub Agentic Workflows
author: GitHub
description: GitHub Agentic Workflows: write repository automation in Markdown, and gh-aw compiles it to Actions that run an agent read-only in a sandbox, with writes going through validated 'safe outputs'. A safer pattern for CI agents. Install the gh extension and follow its create guide.
use_case: Write a Markdown workflow that has an agent triage every new issue nightly, with any labels or comments going through validated safe outputs instead of direct write access.
safety_notes: Official; agent jobs are read-only and sandboxed, writes go through validated safe outputs

name: MarkItDown
author: Microsoft
description: MarkItDown is a lightweight Python tool that converts PDF, Word, PowerPoint, Excel, HTML, images, audio and more into clean Markdown that LLMs handle well, with an optional MCP server. Ideal for feeding documents to agents. Install with `pip install 'markitdown[all]'` and run `markitdown file.pdf`.
use_case: Convert a folder of customer PDFs, slide decks and spreadsheets to Markdown so an agent can summarize them without choking on binary formats.
safety_notes: Official; README warns it reads anything the process can, so sanitize inputs
works_with: Claude Code; Codex; Cursor; OpenCode; Gemini CLI; Grok Bot / any MCP client

name: MCP reference servers
author: Model Context Protocol
description: The MCP steering group's small set of reference servers (filesystem, git, fetch, memory, time and others), meant to demonstrate the protocol. They are educational examples, not production servers; for discovery, use the MCP Registry. Run any with npx or uvx, e.g. `npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-memory`.
use_case: Study the filesystem or git reference server to see how a minimal, correct MCP server is structured before writing your own.
safety_notes: Official reference; scope filesystem paths tightly
works_with: Claude Code; Codex; Cursor; OpenCode; Gemini CLI; Grok Bot / any MCP client

name: FastMCP
author: Prefect (Jeremiah Lowin)
description: FastMCP is the leading Python framework for building MCP servers, clients and apps: declare tools as functions and it handles schemas, transports, auth and deployment. Core if you build MCP servers in Python. Install with `uv add fastmcp`.
use_case: Wrap your product's internal API as an MCP server by decorating a few Python functions, then expose it to any MCP client with auth.
safety_notes: Well-known; clean scan

name: OpenAI Agents SDK
author: OpenAI
description: The OpenAI Agents SDK is a small Python framework for agents with tools, handoffs, guardrails, sessions, tracing, sandbox agents and voice, and it works with 100+ models beyond OpenAI. A solid base for building agent products. Install with `pip install openai-agents`.
use_case: Build a support agent that hands off billing questions to a specialist agent, with guardrails on input and a trace of every step.
safety_notes: Official; clean scan
accounts_needed: OpenAI or other model API key

name: Playwright CLI
author: Microsoft
description: Microsoft's Playwright CLI exposes common browser actions, recording and selector inspection as shell commands with bundled skills, which the Playwright team says is more token-efficient than MCP for coding agents. Pairs with Playwright MCP. Install with `npm install -g @playwright/cli@latest`.
use_case: Have a coding agent record a browser session and generate a Playwright test from it using shell commands instead of an MCP connection.
safety_notes: Official; clean scan
works_with: Claude Code; Codex; Cursor; OpenCode; Gemini CLI

name: Spec Kit
author: GitHub
description: GitHub's Spec Kit gives coding agents a structured spec-driven process (spec, plan, tasks, implement), plus optional bug-fix and idea-evaluation flows, with templates that leave a written record. Useful when features are big enough to need a spec first. Install the CLI with `uv tool install specify-cli` and run `specify init`.
use_case: For a multi-day feature, generate a written spec, plan and task list first, then let the agent implement task by task against that record.
safety_notes: Official; commands tell agents to ignore instructions in fetched pages
works_with: Claude Code; Codex; Cursor; OpenCode; Gemini CLI

name: Kilo Code
author: Kilo Code
description: Kilo Code is an open-source coding agent that runs in VS Code, JetBrains and a terminal CLI, with 500+ models to choose from and open, pass-through pricing. It adds modes, orchestration and a hosted platform on top; the README states the Kilo CLI is a fork of OpenCode. It is for teams that want one agent across editors. Install the editor extension from the marketplace or `npm install -g @kilocode/cli`.
use_case: Use orchestrator mode in VS Code to split a feature into architect, code and debug subtasks across 500+ models.
safety_notes: Company repo with 1,200+ contributors; hits are CI deploy steps, secret-scanner tests and a dev-only postinstall. Its CLI is a declared fork of OpenCode. --auto is off by default; its server can bind 0.0.0.0 via mDNS; telemetry is optional (telemetry.telemetryLevel).
accounts_needed: Kilo account or own model keys
related_note: Kilo CLI is a declared fork of OpenCode

name: Langfuse
author: Langfuse
description: An open-source AI engineering platform for tracing, evals, prompt management, cost tracking and now versioned skill management, built on OpenTelemetry. Self-host or use Langfuse Cloud. Add the SDK to your app and send traces.
use_case: Trace every LLM call in your agent product to find which step burns the most tokens, then run evals on a dataset before shipping a prompt change.
safety_notes: Well-known; self-host to keep traces in-house
install: docker compose up (self-host) or pip install langfuse
accounts_needed: Langfuse Cloud account or self-hosted stack

name: Pi
author: Mario Zechner / Earendil Works
description: Pi is a deliberately minimal coding-agent harness: a unified LLM API, agent loop, TUI and CLI that you extend with packages (skills, prompt templates, extensions) instead of built-in features like sub-agents. It can be driven interactively, in JSON/print mode or over RPC. Install with `npm install -g --ignore-scripts @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent`.
use_case: Build a stripped-down coding agent setup with only the extensions you choose, for a harness you fully understand and can script.
safety_notes: Known authors; install script is their own; recommends --ignore-scripts for npm. Core sandbox, approval and telemetry defaults unknown; pi.dev documents running Pi in a container.

name: pstack
author: Lauren Tan (@poteto), Cursor
description: Cursor's official plugin repository: each folder is a plugin (skills, rules, MCP config) with a manifest, including Lauren Tan's pstack, the source of several skills in this very Grok Bot setup. Use it to add vetted workflow skills (verification, review, formal checks) to Cursor; the skills are plain SKILL.md files, so other agents can read them too. Install from Cursor's plugin marketplace or copy the skill folders.
use_case: Add pstack to Cursor so the agent follows the same plan-first, verify-before-done engineering habits on every task.
safety_notes: Official Cursor repo; docs-only skills; one skill points to Tailscale's official installer. Every listing is manually reviewed per Cursor docs; no root LICENSE; also ships a .claude-plugin manifest.
ease_note: One-click in Cursor; others need a copy or the skills CLI

name: Trail of Bits skills
author: Trail of Bits
description: Trail of Bits' marketplace of security skills and plugins: vulnerability hunting, static analysis helpers, audit workflows and secure development checks. It comes from one of the most respected security firms. Install with `/plugin marketplace add trailofbits/skills` in Claude Code or Codex.
use_case: Before a release, have the agent hunt for vulnerabilities in a module using Trail of Bits' audit workflows and static-analysis helpers.
safety_notes: Top security firm; scan hits are attack examples in docs

name: Beads
author: Gas Town Hall (Steve Yegge)
description: Beads (`bd`) replaces ad-hoc markdown plans with a git-friendly, Dolt-backed graph of issues and dependencies that agents create, claim and close, so long-horizon work survives context resets and can be shared between agents. Install with `brew install beads` and add its instructions to AGENTS.md.
use_case: On a multi-week refactor, let agents file, claim and close dependent issues in a git-tracked graph so work survives context resets.
safety_notes: Known author; clean scan; installers are its own
works_with: Claude Code; Codex; Cursor; OpenCode; Gemini CLI

name: Marketing Skills
author: Corey Haines
description: 53 marketing skills from SaaS marketer Corey Haines: conversion optimization, landing-page copy, SEO, ads, analytics, lead magnets and launch work, with evals. Built for technical founders who want agents to help with growth. Install with `npx skills add coreyhaines31/marketingskills`.
use_case: Before launch, have the agent rewrite your landing page copy and audit its SEO using conversion-focused marketing skills.
safety_notes: Docs plus evals; injection hits are its own defenses and test cases
works_with: Claude Code; Codex; Cursor; OpenCode; Gemini CLI

name: Stagehand
author: Browserbase
description: Stagehand is a TypeScript and Python SDK for browser agents: write normal Playwright-style code and use natural-language `act`, `extract` and `observe` steps where selectors are brittle, with structured outputs via Zod. It runs locally or on Browserbase's cloud. Install with `npm i @browserbasehq/stagehand` or `pip install stagehand`.
use_case: Scrape pricing from competitor sites whose markup changes often by using natural-language extract() steps instead of brittle selectors.
safety_notes: Official Browserbase SDK; cookies persist in a local profile folder, so guard that folder
accounts_needed: Model API key; Browserbase account for cloud browsers

name: Aider
author: Aider AI (Paul Gauthier)
description: Aider is one of the original terminal coding agents: you chat with an LLM inside your git repo and it edits files, builds a repo map for context, and auto-commits each change with a sensible message. It works with almost any cloud or local model and suits people who like a git-first, review-every-diff loop. Install with `python -m pip install aider-install` then `aider-install`, and run `aider` in a repo.
use_case: Chat with Aider in your repo to make a change across several files and get one clean git commit per edit you can review or revert.
safety_notes: Long-running, widely used open-source project; installer hits are its own documented install scripts. Last commit May 2026, so slower than peers now. --yes-always auto-confirms prompts including the analytics opt-in; use --analytics-disable. No OS sandbox. Repo stale about 6 months.

name: Chrome DevTools MCP
author: Google Chrome
description: Chrome DevTools for agents: an MCP server and CLI that let an agent control a live Chrome, read console and network, record performance traces and debug pages. Great for frontend debugging. Install with `npm i chrome-devtools-mcp@latest -g` or the Claude plugin; usage stats go to Google unless disabled.
use_case: When a page loads slowly, have the agent record a performance trace and read console and network logs to find the blocking request.
safety_notes: Official, but usage statistics go to Google by default (--no-usage-statistics turns them off)
works_with: Claude Code; Codex; Cursor; OpenCode; Gemini CLI; Grok Bot / any MCP client

name: Claude Code
author: Anthropic
description: Anthropic's agentic coding tool for the terminal and IDEs: it reads your repo, edits files, runs commands, and supports skills, plugins, hooks, subagents and MCP. This repo holds the changelog, issues, plugins and example settings rather than the source. Install with Anthropic's native installer or npm, then run `claude` in a repo.
use_case: Have Claude Code implement a feature across your repo with plugins, hooks and subagents, then open the PR.
safety_notes: Official, but proprietary license (all rights reserved). Interactive sessions start in auto mode (a classifier approves actions) on v2.1.283+; metrics telemetry is on by default on the Claude API (DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1); the Bash sandbox is opt-in. -p and the SDK start in default mode, which denies anything needing approval
accounts_needed: Claude subscription or Anthropic API key

name: Codex plugin for Claude Code
author: OpenAI
description: A Claude Code plugin that adds /codex:review, /codex:adversarial-review and /codex:rescue, so Claude can hand work to Codex or have Codex cross-review its changes. It is for people who run both agents and want a second model's review on every PR. Install it from the Claude Code plugin marketplace and sign in to Codex.
use_case: Before merging a PR written by Claude, run /codex:adversarial-review to get a second model's critique of the diff.
safety_notes: Official OpenAI; scan clean. Sends your code to OpenAI under your ChatGPT or API account
accounts_needed: ChatGPT plan or OpenAI key for Codex

name: DeepEval
author: Confident AI
description: DeepEval is a Pytest-style framework for unit-testing LLM apps and agents with metrics like G-Eval, task completion, hallucination and tool correctness, running locally. Good for regression tests on prompts and agents. Install with `pip install -U deepeval`.
use_case: Add pytest-style tests that check your agent calls the right tools and doesn't hallucinate, and run them on every commit.
safety_notes: Well-known; the only postinstall hook builds its docs site

name: Docker MCP Gateway
author: Docker
description: Docker's MCP CLI plugin and Gateway: run catalog MCP servers in isolated containers behind one gateway with secrets management. It reduces the risk of running third-party servers. Use via Docker Desktop's MCP Toolkit or the `docker mcp` CLI.
use_case: Run third-party MCP servers each in its own container behind one gateway, so a compromised server can't read your home directory.
safety_notes: Official; container isolation reduces MCP risk
works_with: Claude Code; Codex; Cursor; OpenCode; Gemini CLI; Grok Bot / any MCP client

name: E2B
author: E2B
description: E2B gives agents isolated cloud sandboxes (Firecracker microVMs) to run generated code, shell commands and even full desktops, controlled from JS or Python SDKs. It is a common back end for code interpreters and computer-use demos. Install with `npm i e2b` or `pip install e2b` and set E2B_API_KEY.
use_case: Let your product's agent run user-submitted Python in a disposable cloud microVM instead of on your own servers.
safety_notes: Well-known; code runs in E2B's cloud VMs, not your machine; needs an API key

name: LLM CLI
author: Simon Willison
description: Simon Willison's CLI and Python library for talking to almost any LLM, remote or local, logging everything to SQLite, with plugins, embeddings, structured extraction and tool use. A great Unix-style building block for scripts. Install with `pip install llm` or `brew install llm`.
use_case: Pipe a git diff into a one-line shell command to get a commit message, with every prompt and response logged to SQLite.
safety_notes: Respected author; clean scan
accounts_needed: Model API keys or local models

name: Vercel agent skills
author: Vercel
description: Vercel's official skills, including React and Next.js best practices, web design guidelines and a Vercel optimization audit that starts from real project metrics. Best for Next.js and Vercel projects. Install with `npx skills add vercel-labs/agent-skills`.
use_case: Have the agent review a Next.js app against React best practices and Vercel performance guidance before deploying.
safety_notes: Official; docs-only
works_with: Claude Code; Codex; Cursor; OpenCode; Gemini CLI

name: Agent Package Manager
author: Microsoft
description: APM, Microsoft's Agent Package Manager: one manifest describes the skills, prompts, plugins and MCP servers a project needs, and one command reproduces them across Copilot, Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and others, with org policy. A package.json for agent context. Install the CLI and run `apm install`.
use_case: Pin the exact skills and MCP servers a repo needs in one manifest so every teammate's agent gets the same setup with one command.
safety_notes: Official Microsoft; installs from git sources you choose
works_with: Claude Code; Codex; Cursor; OpenCode; Gemini CLI
ease_note: New CLI and manifest to learn

name: Claude Code Action
author: Anthropic
description: The official GitHub Action that runs Claude Code on PRs and issues: answer @claude mentions, implement changes, review code or run scripted automation, with API, Bedrock, Vertex or Foundry auth. Core for agent-in-CI workflows. Add the workflow YAML and secrets.
use_case: Comment "@claude fix the flaky test" on a PR and let the action push a fix commit to that branch.
safety_notes: Official, but it runs an agent in CI with repo write tokens

name: Helicone
author: Helicone
description: Helicone is an AI gateway plus observability platform: route requests to 100+ models through one OpenAI-compatible endpoint with fallbacks, and log traces, sessions, cost and latency for agents. Integration is a one-line base-URL change in most SDKs, and the whole stack can be self-hosted. It is for teams that want cost and trace visibility quickly. Use the hosted service or self-host with Docker, then point your SDK's base URL at it.
use_case: Route all model calls through one endpoint with automatic fallback to another provider, and see cost per user session.
safety_notes: Company repo; prompt-injection hit is an example string. As a proxy it sees every prompt and key, so self-host or trust the vendor
install: Point your OpenAI-compatible base URL at Helicone's gateway (see README)

name: Logfire SDK
author: Pydantic
description: Logfire is Pydantic's OpenTelemetry-based observability SDK with instrumentations for Pydantic AI, OpenAI, Anthropic, FastAPI and more. Install with `pip install logfire`, run `logfire auth`, and call `logfire.configure()`; it can also export to any OTel backend.
use_case: Trace a Pydantic AI agent and FastAPI backend together to see where a slow request spends its time.
safety_notes: Official Pydantic; SDK is MIT but the default destination is Logfire's cloud (needs a write token); backend is closed-source (UNVERIFIED detail)
accounts_needed: Logfire account or own OTel backend

name: Matt Pocock skills
author: Matt Pocock (@mattpocockuk)
description: Matt Pocock's small, composable engineering skills, explicitly designed as an alternative to process-owning frameworks like GSD, BMAD and Spec Kit. Each skill is short and easy to adapt, so you keep control of the workflow. Install with `npx skills add mattpocock/skills`.
use_case: Drop in one small skill, such as a TypeScript refactor checklist, and edit it to fit your workflow instead of adopting a whole framework.
safety_notes: Docs-only; no hooks or scripts flagged
works_with: Claude Code; Codex; Cursor; OpenCode; Gemini CLI
ease_note: One npx command; works with most agents

name: MCP Toolbox for Databases
author: Google
description: Google's MCP Toolbox for Databases: a prebuilt MCP server for Postgres, MySQL, BigQuery, Spanner and many others, plus a framework for defining safe, parameterized custom tools. Good for giving agents controlled DB access. Run with `npx @toolbox-sdk/server --config tools.yaml` or brew.
use_case: Give an agent read-only, parameterized queries against your production Postgres so it can answer "how many signups last week" without raw SQL access.
safety_notes: Official Google; scope the database credentials
works_with: Claude Code; Codex; Cursor; OpenCode; Gemini CLI; Grok Bot / any MCP client

name: OpenSpec
author: Fission AI
description: OpenSpec is a lightweight, iterative spec framework for coding agents with slash commands to explore, propose and apply changes, built for brownfield code. A lighter alternative to Spec Kit. Install with `npm install -g @fission-ai/openspec@latest` (or its shell installer).
use_case: On an existing codebase, propose a change as a spec delta, review it, then apply it so the spec and code stay in sync.
safety_notes: Clean scan; installs from its own npm package and GitHub
works_with: Claude Code; Codex; Cursor; OpenCode; Gemini CLI

name: Phoenix
author: Arize AI
description: Arize Phoenix is an open-source platform for tracing, evaluation, datasets and experiments on LLM apps, OpenTelemetry-based. Similar role to Langfuse. Install with `pip install arize-phoenix` or use `npx @arizeai/phoenix-cli setup`.
use_case: Run Phoenix locally, trace a RAG agent's retrieval and generation steps, and compare two prompt versions on a saved dataset.
safety_notes: Well-known; token hits are Daytona doc examples calling api.github.com

name: skills CLI (npx skills)
author: Vercel
description: The `skills` CLI (skills.sh) that installs Agent Skills from any GitHub repo into Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode and 75+ other agents, per project or globally. It has become the common installer for most packs in this library. Run `npx skills add owner/repo`.
use_case: Install a skill pack from any GitHub repo into Claude Code, Codex and Cursor at once with one command.
safety_notes: Tool is clean, but it installs whatever repo you point it at
works_with: Claude Code; Codex; Cursor; OpenCode; Gemini CLI

name: Anthropic Agent Skills
author: Anthropic
description: Anthropic's reference skills and the origin of the Agent Skills format: document skills (docx, pptx, xlsx, pdf), frontend design, MCP builder, skill creator and more. It is the best example of how to write skills well. Install via `/plugin marketplace add anthropics/skills` or copy folders into any skills-aware agent.
use_case: Before writing your own skill, copy Anthropic's skill-creator or docx skill as a template for structure and progressive disclosure.
safety_notes: Official; scan hits are defensive guidance only. README says demonstration and educational purposes; no root license, per-skill LICENSE.txt (docx/pdf/pptx/xlsx moved to Apache-2.0 on 6 Nov 2026).
works_with: Claude Code; Codex; Cursor; OpenCode; Gemini CLI

name: Claude Cookbooks
author: Anthropic
description: Official notebooks and recipes for building with Claude: agent patterns, tool use, the Agent SDK, skills, context and memory, and OpenTelemetry tracing. Read or run the notebooks you need.
use_case: Run the memory or tool-use notebook to learn a pattern before building it into your product.
safety_notes: Official Anthropic; educational; one README uses the astral.sh uv curl|sh installer; repo carries its own secret-audit skill
accounts_needed: Anthropic API key for running notebooks

name: Claude Plugins (official)
author: Anthropic
description: Anthropic's curated directory of Claude Code plugins: internal plugins under /plugins and partner or community ones under /external_plugins. Use it as the default, policy-reviewed place to discover plugins. Install anything with `/plugin install name@claude-plugins-official`.
use_case: Browse the official directory to find a vetted plugin, such as a code-review or LSP plugin, instead of installing an unknown repo.
safety_notes: Policy-reviewed directory; anything under external_plugins is third-party, so read it first. Auto-added to Claude Code; CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_OFFICIAL_MARKETPLACE_AUTOINSTALL turns that off.

name: Cognee
author: Topoteretes
description: Cognee is an open-source memory platform that turns documents, code and conversations into a self-hosted knowledge graph plus vectors that agents can search across sessions. It runs locally with small CPU models and no API key, and has an MCP server and integrations. It is for builders who want graph-backed memory without a hosted service. Install with `pip install cognee` (or `uv pip install cognee`) and call add, cognify and search.
use_case: Turn your docs and code into a local knowledge graph the agent can query for "what depends on this service".
safety_notes: Company repo; credential mentions are code that avoids indexing secret files and CI test setup

name: Deep Agents
author: LangChain (Harrison Chase)
description: LangChain's batteries-included agent harness on LangGraph: planning, sub-agents, file system, long-horizon defaults, model-agnostic, with LangSmith tracing. A fast start for building your own agents. Install with `uv add deepagents`.
use_case: Prototype a research agent that plans, spawns sub-agents and writes files, without building the loop from scratch.
safety_notes: Official LangChain; installer hits point to astral.sh

name: Docling
author: Docling Project (started at IBM Research)
description: Docling parses PDFs and many other formats with layout analysis, reading order, table structure, formulas and OCR into a unified document model, then exports Markdown or JSON for RAG and agents. Heavier but more accurate than MarkItDown on complex PDFs. Install with `pip install docling`.
use_case: Parse scanned financial PDFs with tables and formulas into structured JSON for a RAG pipeline where MarkItDown loses the layout.
safety_notes: IBM-originated open project; downloads layout models on first use
works_with: Claude Code; Codex; Cursor; OpenCode; Gemini CLI; Grok Bot / any MCP client
ease_note: pip; models download on first run

name: MCP Scanner
author: Cisco AI Defense
description: Cisco's Python tool that scans MCP servers and tools with YARA rules, LLM analysis and the optional Cisco AI Defense API to flag malicious tools. Works offline with YARA only. Install with `uv tool install cisco-ai-mcp-scanner`.
use_case: Before adding a new MCP server to your config, scan its tool descriptions offline for hidden instructions or malicious patterns.
safety_notes: Official Cisco; the base64 and exec hits are attack samples in its own evals
accounts_needed: None for YARA mode; Cisco AI Defense key optional
ease_note: uv tool install; config for engines

name: Microsoft Agent Framework
author: Microsoft
description: A Python and .NET framework for agents and graph-based multi-agent workflows with OpenTelemetry tracing built in. Install with `pip install agent-framework` or the NuGet packages.
use_case: Build a .NET multi-agent workflow with graph-based routing and OpenTelemetry tracing for an enterprise app.
safety_notes: Official Microsoft. Adds a feature-usage bitmask to its User-Agent (opt out with AGENT_FRAMEWORK_USER_AGENT_DISABLED or AGENT_FRAMEWORK_FEATURE_MASK_DISABLED). Successor to Semantic Kernel and AutoGen (UNVERIFIED this pass)

name: OpenInference
author: Arize AI
description: OpenTelemetry semantic conventions plus auto-instrumentation packages for LLM and agent frameworks in Python, JS and Java. It is what Phoenix uses under the hood and works with any OTel backend. Install the instrumentor for your framework from pip or npm.
use_case: Auto-instrument a LangChain or OpenAI app so every LLM call shows up in Phoenix or another OTel backend.
safety_notes: Arize org; its own triage skill tells agents to ignore injected instructions; phoenix-cli skill reads PHOENIX_API_KEY

name: OpenLLMetry
author: Traceloop (ServiceNow)
description: OpenLLMetry is a set of OpenTelemetry instrumentations for LLM providers, vector DBs and agent frameworks, so LLM calls show up as standard traces in Datadog, Honeycomb, Grafana or any OTel backend. Its semantic conventions were upstreamed into OpenTelemetry. It is for people who already run OTel and want agent traces there instead of a separate tool. Install with `pip install traceloop-sdk` and call `Traceloop.init()`.
use_case: Make LLM calls show up as spans in the Datadog or Grafana you already use, next to your normal API traces.
safety_notes: Company repo; one prompt-injection hit is a guardrail test sample. The Traceloop SDK sends to Traceloop's cloud when an API key is set; point the exporter at your own OTel endpoint otherwise.

name: shadcn/ui
author: shadcn
description: shadcn/ui is a set of accessible React components you copy into your project and own, plus a CLI and registry (with an MCP server) that coding agents use to add components correctly. It is the default UI kit for many agent-built apps. Run `npx shadcn@latest init` in a React project.
use_case: Ask the agent to add a data table and dialog to your React app; it pulls the real shadcn components from the registry rather than inventing markup.
safety_notes: Well-known; postinstall only builds docs
works_with: Claude Code; Codex; Cursor; OpenCode; Gemini CLI; Grok Bot / any MCP client

name: DSPy
author: Stanford NLP
description: DSPy is a framework for programming language models with signatures and modules instead of hand-written prompts, plus optimizers that compile and tune prompts against your metrics. Install with `pip install dspy`.
use_case: Replace a hand-tuned classification prompt with a DSPy module and let the optimizer tune it against labeled examples.
safety_notes: Large, well-known academic project; scan clean. Origin details (Omar Khattab et al.) UNVERIFIED this pass

name: garak
author: NVIDIA
description: NVIDIA's LLM vulnerability scanner, an nmap-style tool that probes apps for prompt injection, jailbreaks, data leakage, hallucination and toxic output. Useful to red-team your own agent's model endpoints. Install with `pip install -U garak` and point it at a model or API.
use_case: Point garak at your agent's model endpoint before launch to probe for prompt injection, jailbreaks and data leakage.
safety_notes: Official NVIDIA; the injection text is test probes
accounts_needed: Access to the model endpoint you test

name: Inspect
author: UK AI Security Institute
description: Inspect, the UK AI Security Institute's framework for LLM and agent evaluations, with tool use, sandboxes, model-graded scoring and 200+ prebuilt evals. Strong for serious agent benchmarking. Install with pip and write evals in Python.
use_case: Benchmark your agent on a sandboxed coding eval from the 200+ prebuilt suite and compare scores across model versions.
safety_notes: Government AI safety lab; clean scan

name: Laminar
author: Laminar
description: Laminar is an open-source observability platform aimed at agents: one line of code traces Vercel AI SDK, Browser Use, Stagehand, LangChain, OpenAI, Anthropic and more, and 'signals' let you describe a behavior in plain English (for example 'agent is stuck in a loop') and get pinged when it happens. It also has an evals SDK and CLI for CI. It is for agent builders, especially browser agents. Install with `pip install 'lmnr[all]'` or npm, then initialize with a project key.
use_case: Trace a Browser Use agent and set a plain-English signal such as "agent got stuck in a loop" to flag bad runs.
safety_notes: Small company repo; one installer hit in docs; nothing risky

name: Serena
author: Oraios AI
description: Serena is a coding-agent toolkit that exposes semantic, language-server-based code navigation and editing (find symbol, references, insert after symbol) over MCP. It makes agents more precise on large codebases. Run with uvx and add to your MCP client.
use_case: In a large codebase, let the agent rename a function and update every reference through language-server symbol lookups instead of text search.
safety_notes: Well-known; clean scan
works_with: Claude Code; Codex; Cursor; OpenCode; Gemini CLI; Grok Bot / any MCP client

name: Basic Memory
author: Basic Machines
description: Basic Memory gives Claude, Codex, Cursor and other MCP clients a persistent knowledge base stored as plain Markdown files on your machine, which you can also open in Obsidian. Agents write notes and links during conversations and read them back later through an MCP server. It is for people who want durable, human-readable agent memory. Install with `uv tool install basic-memory` and add it as an MCP server; a paid cloud tier also exists.
use_case: Have the agent write decisions and project notes as Markdown files you can open in Obsidian, then recall them in the next session.
safety_notes: Small company; installer hits are its own docs; AGPL-3.0 license matters if you embed it in a product
works_with: Claude Code; Codex; Cursor; OpenCode; Gemini CLI; Grok Bot / any MCP client

name: ccusage
author: ryoppippi
description: ccusage reads the local usage logs of Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Amp and others and prints daily, weekly, monthly and per-session token and cost reports. Handy for tracking agent spend. Run `npx ccusage@latest`.
use_case: At the end of the month, run one command to see which days and sessions drove your Claude Code and Codex spend.
safety_notes: Reads local log files only; MIT

name: Cline
author: Cline
description: Cline is an open-source autonomous coding agent available as a VS Code and JetBrains extension, a desktop app, a CLI for headless CI use and an SDK, with plan/act modes, MCP support and per-step approval. Bring your own model keys. Install from the marketplace or `npm i -g cline`.
use_case: Work in VS Code with an agent that proposes a plan, then edits files and runs commands only after you approve each step.
safety_notes: Well-known; human-in-the-loop approvals by default. CLI --auto-approve defaults to true (ACP mode false); telemetry on by default (set telemetryOptOut: true); no shell allow/deny list, so block commands with a PreToolUse hook; the extension's YOLO setting approves everything.

name: Browser Use
author: Browser Use
description: Browser Use is an open-source browser agent: give it a task and the model writes Python in a persistent REPL against Chrome DevTools Protocol helpers to complete it, locally or on Browser Use Cloud. It also ships a skill for coding agents. Install with `uv tool install browser-use` and `browser-use skill install`.
use_case: Give an agent a task such as "find the cheapest flight on these dates" and let it drive Chrome to complete it.
safety_notes: Legit, but it drives real logged-in browsers and the cloud offers stealth/CAPTCHA solving; use a separate profile
accounts_needed: Model API key; Browser Use Cloud optional

name: Claude Quickstarts
author: Anthropic
description: Anthropic's collection of starter projects for the Claude API: customer support agent, financial data analyst, the computer-use reference demo (Docker desktop the model controls) and agent examples. Good for reading how Anthropic structures agent loops. Clone a quickstart and follow its README with an API key.
use_case: Clone the computer-use demo to see exactly how Anthropic wires a model to a sandboxed desktop before building your own.
safety_notes: Official; the computer-use demo runs inside a Docker container

name: Cloudflare Sandbox SDK
author: Cloudflare
description: The Sandbox SDK runs untrusted or generated code in a Linux container owned by one user, task or session, driven from a Cloudflare Worker, with file streaming, S3 mounts and egress control. Good for hosting agent code execution at the edge. Install `@cloudflare/sandbox` in a Workers project.
use_case: Run each user's agent-generated code in its own container driven from a Worker, with egress limited to approved hosts.
safety_notes: Official; your Worker controls network egress and credentials

name: Mem0
author: Mem0
description: Mem0 adds long-term memory to agents: it extracts facts from conversations, stores them, and retrieves the relevant ones on later turns, with published LoCoMo and LongMemEval benchmarks. Use the open-source library, self-host with Docker, or use the hosted platform; there are Python and TypeScript SDKs, a CLI and an MCP server. It is for agent products that need per-user memory. Install with `pip install mem0ai` or `npm install mem0ai`.
use_case: Let your product's assistant remember each user's preferences across chats so it stops asking the same questions.
safety_notes: Company repo; installer hits are its own docs. The managed platform stores memories on Mem0 servers, so self-host for private data. PostHog telemetry is on by default in the SDK and CLI; set MEM0_TELEMETRY=False.
ease_note: pip/npm SDK; LLM and vector store config

name: Probity
author: Nizar Selander
description: Probity hooks into your coding agent and checks every file write and shell command before it runs; if an action breaks a rule it blocks it and tells the agent why. It ships a built-in Test-Driven Development rule, can block destructive commands, and lets you write custom rules in a few lines of TypeScript, with one config working across most agents. It is the successor to the author's TDD Guard. Install with `npm install -D @nizos/probity` and add its hook config.
use_case: Block your coding agent from running destructive commands such as rm -rf or force-push, and enforce test-first on every file write.
safety_notes: Small but real maintainer (creator of TDD Guard); hooks only intercept agent writes and commands; no risky patterns
ease_note: npm dev dependency plus hook setup

name: Strands Agent SOPs
author: AWS (Strands Agents)
description: Agent SOPs are Markdown standard operating procedures with RFC-2119 MUST/SHOULD steps, parameters and resumable progress. Use them as system prompts, serve them through the bundled MCP server, or export them as Agent Skills. It is a structured way to make agents follow repeatable workflows.
use_case: Write a release checklist as an SOP with MUST steps and serve it over MCP so any agent follows it step by step and can resume.
safety_notes: Docs plus a small Python package; scan clean. GitHub org is not verified, but the AWS Open Source Blog announced it
works_with: Claude Code; Codex; Cursor; OpenCode; Gemini CLI; Grok Bot / any MCP client

name: Cloudflare MCP servers
author: Cloudflare
description: A set of Cloudflare-hosted remote MCP servers (docs, Workers bindings, observability, Radar, browser rendering and more) that let an agent read and change your Cloudflare account. Authentication is OAuth-scoped per server. Add the server URL you need to any MCP client.
use_case: Ask the agent why a Worker started erroring, and let it read the observability logs and bindings on your account.
safety_notes: Official; OAuth-scoped remote servers
works_with: Claude Code; Codex; Cursor; OpenCode; Gemini CLI; Grok Bot / any MCP client

name: Container Use
author: Dagger
description: Container Use is an MCP server and CLI that gives each coding agent its own container and git branch, so several agents can work in parallel without clobbering your checkout; you review and merge their branches. Works with Claude Code, Cursor and other MCP agents. Install with `brew install dagger/tap/container-use`.
use_case: Run three agents on three features at once, each in its own container and git branch, then review and merge only the good ones.
safety_notes: Well-known (Dagger, founded by Docker's creator); agents work in containers
works_with: Claude Code; Codex; Cursor; OpenCode; Gemini CLI; Grok Bot / any MCP client

name: Defuddle
author: Steph Ango (kepano)
description: Defuddle removes clutter (nav, sidebars, comments, footers) from a web page and returns the main content as clean HTML or Markdown, as used by Obsidian Web Clipper. A lightweight Readability alternative for feeding pages to agents. Run `npx defuddle parse https://example.com/article` or use the library.
use_case: Strip nav bars and comments from a long article so you feed the agent only the main text as clean Markdown.
safety_notes: Clean scan; small library from Obsidian's CEO

name: Grafana MCP
author: Grafana Labs
description: Grafana's MCP server for dashboards, Prometheus and Loki queries, alerts, incidents and more. Useful for agents that investigate production issues. Run with `uvx mcp-grafana` or Docker and a service-account token.
use_case: During an incident, have the agent query Loki logs and Prometheus metrics for the failing service and summarize what changed.
safety_notes: Official; clean scan
works_with: Claude Code; Codex; Cursor; OpenCode; Gemini CLI; Grok Bot / any MCP client

name: HumanLayer
author: HumanLayer
description: HumanLayer runs Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and Pi sessions on your machines and lets you steer them from a desktop or web app: tasks, sessions, plans and reviews synced through a daemon on each host. Aimed at managing many agents at once. Install the desktop app or `humanlayer` CLI per the docs.
use_case: Kick off several Claude Code and Codex sessions on your machines and steer or approve them from one web app while away from your desk.
safety_notes: Clean scan; known team (12-factor-agents)

name: AGENTS.md
author: AGENTS.md project
description: AGENTS.md is an open format for a single 'README for agents' file at the root of a repo, holding build, test and style instructions. Codex, Cursor, Goose, Grok, Copilot and others read it by default, and Gemini CLI and Claude Code can be pointed at it. Add one AGENTS.md and keep CLAUDE.md as a one-line `@AGENTS.md` shim.
use_case: Write one AGENTS.md with build, test and style rules so Codex, Cursor, Grok and Claude Code all follow the same instructions.
safety_notes: Spec and website only (MIT, has a technical charter); the site uses Vercel Analytics. Org identity is UNVERIFIED beyond agents.md itself
works_with: Claude Code; Codex; Cursor; OpenCode; Gemini CLI

name: BMAD Method
author: BMad Code
description: BMad Method is an agile, AI-driven development process with agent personas (analyst, PM, architect, dev, QA) that carry briefs, specs and architecture forward. It sizes itself from small changes to large systems. Install with `npx bmad-method install`.
use_case: For a new product, have analyst, PM and architect personas produce a brief, PRD and architecture doc before any code is written.
safety_notes: Clean scan
works_with: Claude Code; Codex; Cursor; OpenCode; Gemini CLI

name: Cua
author: Cua (trycua)
description: Cua is an open-source computer-use platform: Cua Driver for desktop automation, Lume for fast macOS/Linux VMs on Apple Silicon, an SDK and CLI for sandboxes, small decision models and Cua Bench for evaluating computer-use agents. It is aimed at people building and testing agents that operate whole computers. Install pieces with the documented scripts, ideally inside a VM.
use_case: Spin up a macOS VM on Apple Silicon and let a computer-use agent test your desktop app's install flow end to end.
safety_notes: Legit project, but the driver controls your real desktop and installs via curl | sh scripts; run it in a VM

name: Gemini CLI
author: Google
description: Gemini CLI is Google's open-source terminal agent with tools, MCP, extensions and skills. As of June 2026 the README says it targets Gemini Code Assist Standard/Enterprise licenses; individual and Google AI Pro/Ultra users moved to Antigravity CLI. Run with `npx @google/gemini-cli` if you have a supported license.
use_case: Use Gemini's long context to have the agent read an entire mid-size repo and explain how a feature flows through it.
safety_notes: Official; README says free and Google AI plans moved to Antigravity CLI. Approval asks by default, but the sandbox is off unless you use --yolo (which turns it on); privacy.usageStatisticsEnabled defaults to true (set false); security.disableYoloMode is available.

name: MCP Registry
author: Model Context Protocol
description: The official MCP Registry service: an app-store-style API listing published MCP servers, with its own publishing flow. Use it to discover servers or publish your own. Browse the live API or run the container locally.
use_case: Look up the official, published package for an MCP server before installing it, or publish your own server so clients can find it.
safety_notes: Official registry code; listed servers are third-party
install: Browse the API, or docker run -p 8080:8080 ghcr.io/modelcontextprotocol/registry:latest

name: NeMo Guardrails
author: NVIDIA
description: NVIDIA's toolkit for adding programmable guardrails ('rails') to LLM apps: topic control, jailbreak and injection checks, fact-checking and output moderation. Useful in a production agent's runtime. Install with `pip install nemoguardrails` and define rails in config.
use_case: Add a rail to your support bot that refuses off-topic requests and blocks jailbreak attempts before they reach the model.
safety_notes: Official NVIDIA; clean scan

name: Opik
author: Comet
description: Opik is Comet's open-source platform for tracing LLM and agent runs, scoring them with LLM-as-judge and heuristic metrics, managing prompts, and monitoring production. The full platform is Apache-2.0 and self-hostable, with a Python SDK, integrations for most frameworks, and an MCP server. It is for teams that want tracing and evals in one place. Install the SDK with `pip install opik` and run `opik configure`, or self-host with Docker.
use_case: Score your agent's production traces with LLM-as-judge metrics and alert when answer quality drops.
safety_notes: Established ML company; hits are a prompt-injection detector metric and docs. Anonymous usage reports on by default; set OPIK_USAGE_REPORT_ENABLED=false when self-hosting privately.
accounts_needed: None to self-host; Comet account for cloud

name: Stripe AI
author: Stripe
description: Stripe's home for agent plugins, skills and benchmarks for building on Stripe; older packages like the agent toolkit and @stripe/mcp are now deprecated in favor of Stripe's hosted MCP. Use it for billing and token-metering work in an agent product. Install skills with `npx skills add https://docs.stripe.com` or connect the hosted MCP.
use_case: Have the agent implement usage-based billing correctly, following Stripe's own skills and calling the hosted Stripe MCP.
safety_notes: Official; skills install the Stripe CLI from cli.stripe.com
works_with: Claude Code; Codex; Cursor; OpenCode; Gemini CLI; Grok Bot / any MCP client

name: Claude Squad
author: smtg-ai
description: Claude Squad is a tmux-based terminal app that manages multiple Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, OpenCode or Aider sessions, each in its own git worktree, so you can run tasks in parallel and review before pushing. Install with `brew install claude-squad`.
use_case: Run Claude Code, Codex and Aider on separate tasks in their own worktrees, flip between them in tmux and review each diff before pushing.
safety_notes: Clean scan; AGPL-3.0; yolo mode is opt-in
works_with: Claude Code; Codex; Gemini CLI; OpenCode

name: DuckDB / MotherDuck MCP
author: MotherDuck
description: A local MCP server that lets agents run SQL with DuckDB against local files, in-memory databases, S3 data or MotherDuck, and browse catalogs. Great for quick analytics on CSV or Parquet without a warehouse. Add with `claude mcp add duckdb -- uvx mcp-server-motherduck --db-path :memory:`.
use_case: Ask the agent questions about a 2 GB Parquet export and let it answer with DuckDB SQL locally, no warehouse needed.
safety_notes: Official; read-only unless you pass --read-write
works_with: Claude Code; Codex; Cursor; OpenCode; Gemini CLI; Grok Bot / any MCP client
install: claude mcp add duckdb -- uvx mcp-server-motherduck --db-path :memory:

name: GPT Researcher
author: Assaf Elovic (Tavily)
description: GPT Researcher is an autonomous agent that splits a question into sub-questions, researches the web or local documents in parallel and produces a long, cited report, with deep-research and multi-agent modes and an MCP server. Good for market or technical research. Install with pip or Docker and set LLM and search API keys.
use_case: Produce a cited 3,000-word market report on a competitor space by letting the agent research sub-questions in parallel.
safety_notes: Respected author; installers are standard
accounts_needed: Model API key + search API key

name: Grok Build
author: xAI
description: Grok Build is xAI's terminal coding harness, with a TUI, a headless `-p` mode and ACP support for editors. It reads AGENTS.md and supports skills and MCP. Install from x.ai/cli or npm and sign in with an xAI account.
use_case: Run Grok as a headless coding agent with -p in a script, with the sandbox turned on.
safety_notes: Official xAI repo (Apache-2.0, periodic monorepo sync, last 29 Sep 2026). Sandbox is off by default; --yolo always approves (deny rules and hooks still apply). Telemetry default unknown; /privacy controls retention. Postinstall only fetches its own binary

name: Letta Code
author: Letta
description: Letta Code is Letta's stateful agent harness and terminal UI, where agents keep long-term memory and improve across sessions; it is now where Letta (formerly MemGPT) is developed. Install with `npm install -g @letta-ai/letta-code`, run `letta`, or `letta server` to self-host.
use_case: Keep one long-lived coding agent that remembers your project's conventions across weeks of sessions.
safety_notes: Official Letta; defaults to Letta cloud (api.letta.com) unless you self-host; needs LETTA_API_KEY. Postinstall applies vendor patches
accounts_needed: Letta Cloud account or self-hosted server

name: PyRIT
author: Microsoft
description: Microsoft AI Red Team's toolkit for finding security and safety weaknesses in generative AI systems through automated scans, multi-turn attacks and human-led testing, with CLI, GUI and Python framework. Good for structured red-team exercises. Install with pip per the docs.
use_case: Run multi-turn automated attacks against your chatbot to measure how often it can be talked into leaking its system prompt.
safety_notes: Official Microsoft; the old Azure/PyRIT copy is archived, use this one

name: security-audit
author: Cloudflare
description: A coding-agent skill that runs a six-phase security audit: reconnaissance, coverage-led hunting, candidate validation, structured findings, independent verification and reporting. It seeded Cloudflare's internal vulnerability-discovery harness. Install with `npx skills add https://github.com/cloudflare/security-audit-skill`.
use_case: Before a security review, have the agent run a six-phase audit of a service and hand you validated findings instead of noise.
safety_notes: Official; docs plus zero-dependency validators; no network calls in code
works_with: Claude Code; Codex; Cursor; OpenCode; Gemini CLI

name: Snyk Agent Scan
author: Snyk (ex-Invariant Labs)
description: Snyk's scanner (formerly Invariant's mcp-scan) that discovers the agents, MCP servers and skills on your machine and checks them for prompt injection, tool poisoning and malware. Useful as a periodic hygiene check. Run with `uvx`; note it sends tool descriptions to Snyk's API.
use_case: Once a month, scan every MCP config and skills folder on your laptop for tool poisoning and prompt injection.
safety_notes: Trusted scanner, but it uploads tool descriptions and skill text (secrets redacted) to Snyk's API

name: Cloudflare skills
author: Cloudflare
description: Cloudflare's skills for building on Workers, the Agents SDK, Durable Objects and the wider developer platform, bundled with the Cloudflare MCP server where plugins are supported. Use it if you deploy agents or APIs on Cloudflare. Install via the Claude or Codex plugin marketplace, or the skills CLI.
use_case: Have the agent build and deploy a Durable Objects–backed agent on Workers using Cloudflare's own patterns.
safety_notes: Official; clean scan

name: Docker Agent
author: Docker
description: Docker Agent (formerly cagent) builds and runs agents from declarative YAML: multi-agent teams, MCP tools and sandboxing from Docker Engineering. It is for people who want agents defined as config and run like containers. Install the CLI and run `docker agent run agent.yaml`.
use_case: Define a reviewer and fixer agent team in one YAML file and run it like a container.
safety_notes: Official Docker (renamed from docker/cagent). Collects usage telemetry by default (documented, can be disabled); has a --yolo / autoApprove mode

name: goose
author: goose (AAIF; originally Block)
description: goose is a general-purpose local agent in Rust with a desktop app, CLI and API, working with 15+ model providers and extensible through MCP extensions and recipes. It handles code, research and automation tasks. Install the desktop app or CLI from the releases or docs.
use_case: Save a recipe that researches a topic, writes a summary and files it, then rerun it locally with any model provider.
