use_case: Install only the product or compliance bundle when a non-engineering task, such as a PRD or a SOC 2 checklist, comes up.
safety_notes: Large single-maintainer set; scan hits were its own security-auditor examples, but read before bulk install

name: Claude Subconscious
author: Letta
description: Hooks that send each Claude Code transcript to a Letta agent, which studies your codebase and the web and 'whispers back' memory before your next prompt. It is an experiment in background memory for coding agents. Install the hooks and set a Letta key.
use_case: Experiment with a background agent that learns your codebase from Claude Code transcripts (self-host Letta first).
safety_notes: Ships every Claude Code session transcript to Letta cloud by default (set LETTA_BASE_URL to self-host); a background agent reads files and searches the web
accounts_needed: Letta API key or self-hosted Letta

name: OpenClaw
author: Peter Steinberger (@steipete) and community
description: OpenClaw is an open-source personal AI assistant that runs on your machine and meets you in 20+ chat apps (Slack, Telegram, WhatsApp and others), with swappable model plugins and local memory. It has broad system access by design. Install with its shell script or npm.
use_case: Message a personal assistant on Telegram to check your calendar and draft replies, running on a machine you control and isolate.
safety_notes: Clean core, but it gets broad system access and its skill marketplace has had malware

name: Antigravity CLI
author: Google (Antigravity)
description: `agy` is the terminal surface of Google's Antigravity 2.0 agent harness. It asks before edits and commands by default, and its auto mode runs commands inside an OS sandbox. Install with the curl script from the README; there is no source here.
use_case: Try Google's Antigravity agent from the terminal, asking before each edit, while comparing it with Gemini CLI.
safety_notes: Official Google, but no LICENSE file (README and changelog only; the binary installs via curl). README: Interactions data is collected by default, opt out in settings. Default mode asks before edits and commands; auto mode sandboxes commands; --dangerously-skip-permissions exists
related_note: Same vendor as Gemini CLI; closed binary

name: AWS MCP Servers
author: AWS
description: AWS Labs' suite of specialized MCP servers for AWS services (docs, CDK, cost, EKS, Lambda and many more), now succeeded by the Agent Toolkit for AWS. Use it if you run on AWS. Each server runs via `uvx`.
use_case: Have the agent estimate the monthly cost of a CDK stack with the AWS cost server (prefer the Agent Toolkit for new setups).
safety_notes: Official AWS; uses your AWS credentials, so give it a limited role
works_with: Claude Code; Codex; Cursor; OpenCode; Gemini CLI; Grok Bot / any MCP client

name: Browserbase skills
author: Browserbase
description: Browserbase's skills that let Claude Code drive remote cloud browsers through the official `browse` CLI, with identity, CAPTCHA solving, proxies, traces and serverless browser functions. Good when local browsers aren't enough. Install via the Claude marketplace or `npx skills add browserbase/skills`; needs a Browserbase account.
use_case: When a site blocks headless local browsers, have the agent drive a remote cloud browser with proxies and CAPTCHA handling.
safety_notes: Official; one skill reads its API key from your keychain or 1Password
works_with: Claude Code; Codex; Cursor; OpenCode; Gemini CLI

name: Obsidian skills
author: Steph Ango (@kepano), Obsidian CEO
description: Skills from Obsidian's CEO that teach agents Obsidian's formats: Markdown flavors, Bases, JSON Canvas and the Obsidian CLI. Useful if your notes, specs or knowledge base live in an Obsidian vault. Install as a Claude marketplace plugin or with `npx skills add`.
use_case: Have the agent build an Obsidian Base that tracks your product specs by status.
safety_notes: Small docs-only set from Obsidian's CEO
works_with: Claude Code; Codex; Cursor; OpenCode; Gemini CLI

name: tstack
author: Theo Browne (@theo)
description: Theo Browne's personal agent skills, cleaned up for Claude Code and Codex. Highlights are full-send (prove, review, file, babysit and merge a PR unattended), council (three models from different providers review until they agree) and loop-style reviewers. Best for people who want aggressive PR automation; install with the skills CLI or copy the folders.
use_case: Hand a small PR to full-send so it proves, reviews and merges it, or ask council for a three-model review on a risky change.
safety_notes: Clean scan, but full-send merges PRs and force-pushes its own branch unattended
ease_note: Copy or skills CLI; some skills prefer T3 Code features

name: Scientific Agent Skills
author: K-Dense AI
description: 177 skills for scientific work: bioinformatics, chemistry, scientific databases, data analysis and literature research, from the K-Dense startup. Valuable for research-heavy tasks, not general product work. Install with `npx skills add K-Dense-AI/scientific-agent-skills`.
use_case: Have the agent pull protein data from a public database and run a sequence analysis for a research question.
safety_notes: Startup-run, not a lab; some skills point at third-party install scripts
works_with: Claude Code; Codex; Cursor; OpenCode; Gemini CLI
ease_note: npx; some skills need extra installs

name: Trail of Bits Claude Code config
author: Trail of Bits
description: Trail of Bits' opinionated Claude Code defaults: permission deny rules for SSH keys and cloud credentials, sandboxing, hooks, local-model setup and workflows. Read it as a hardening reference and copy the parts you want into your settings.
use_case: Copy its deny rules so Claude Code can never read your SSH keys or cloud credentials.
safety_notes: Strong credential deny rules for ~/.ssh and cloud credentials, BUT it recommends a `claude-yolo` alias (--dangerously-skip-permissions) inside its sandbox and uses rustup and LM Studio curl|sh installers. No LICENSE

name: Atlassian MCP Server
author: Atlassian
description: Atlassian's official cloud-hosted MCP server for Jira, Confluence, JSM, Bitbucket, Compass and Loom, OAuth-scoped to your site. Useful if your team tracks work in Jira. Add with `claude mcp add --transport http atlassian https://mcp.atlassian.com/v2/mcp`.
use_case: Ask the agent to summarize all open Jira tickets for a release and update their Confluence release notes.
safety_notes: Official; OAuth-scoped
works_with: Claude Code; Codex; Cursor; OpenCode; Gemini CLI; Grok Bot / any MCP client
install: claude mcp add --transport http atlassian https://mcp.atlassian.com/v2/mcp

name: Awesome MCP Servers
author: Frank Fiegel (punkpeye)
description: A large community list of MCP servers grouped by category, maintained by the founder of the Glama MCP directory. Good for discovering servers; every entry is third-party and unvetted. Browse the README or glama.ai.
use_case: Search the list for a calendar or CRM MCP server, then vet the one you pick before installing.
safety_notes: A list; entries are third-party and unvetted

name: Azure Skills plugin
author: Microsoft
description: Microsoft's Azure plugin that bundles curated Azure skills with MCP-backed execution, so an agent can choose services, validate and deploy real resources. Aimed at teams shipping on Azure. Install via the Claude marketplace (`/plugin install azure@azure-skills`).
use_case: Have the agent choose the right Azure service for a new API, validate the config and deploy it.
safety_notes: Official, but skills create real cloud resources; review plans before approving
related_note: Shares 54 identical SKILL.md files with microsoft/skills

name: Cline Skills
author: Cline
description: The skills Cline's own team uses, in SKILL.md format (for example Railway deploy and database analysis). Cline installs skills through `npx skills`, so these also work in other harnesses.
use_case: Use Cline's Railway deploy skill to have any agent ship a service to Railway.
safety_notes: Official Cline org; hits are Railway SSH how-to docs. Small and young (45 stars)
works_with: Claude Code; Codex; Cursor; OpenCode; Gemini CLI

name: n8n Skills
author: Romuald Czlonkowski
description: Fourteen Claude Code skills plus a router skill and hooks that teach agents to build production-ready n8n workflows with n8n-MCP and deploy self-hosted n8n. Companion to n8n-MCP. Install with `/plugin marketplace add czlonkowski/n8n-skills`.
use_case: Pair with n8n-MCP so the agent follows n8n's expression syntax and validation rules when building workflows.
safety_notes: Clean scan; hooks only enforce its own rules

name: Remotion skills
author: Remotion
description: Remotion's skills for making videos with code: one best-practices skill that covers compositions, animation, audio and rendering. Handy for product demo or launch videos generated by an agent. Install with `npx skills add remotion-dev/skills`; Remotion's own license terms apply.
use_case: Have the agent write a 30-second product demo video in React with Remotion and render it to MP4.
safety_notes: Official; docs-only (Remotion's own license terms apply)
works_with: Claude Code; Codex; Cursor; OpenCode; Gemini CLI

name: Amplifier
author: Microsoft
description: Amplifier is a Microsoft research demonstrator: a modular AI development assistant built from composable modules and agents, successor to the earlier Claude Code-based Amplifier. It is for exploring harness design rather than daily use. Install with uv per the README.
use_case: Explore how a modular AI assistant composes agents and tools, as research for your own harness design.
safety_notes: Official Microsoft, but the README cautions it is a research demonstrator with permissive AI tools; installer path uses astral uv curl|sh / irm|iex

name: Gemini skills
author: Google (Gemini)
description: Agent Skills from Google for building with the Gemini API and SDKs: model selection, interactions and agent patterns, in the standard SKILL.md format. Copy them into your agent's skills folder or install with a skills CLI.
use_case: Have the agent pick the right Gemini model and write correct SDK code for a new feature.
safety_notes: Official Google Gemini org. The gemini-api-cli skill tells the agent to run a curl ... install.sh | bash installer from raw.githubusercontent.com; reads the Gemini API key from env
works_with: Claude Code; Codex; Cursor; OpenCode; Gemini CLI
accounts_needed: Gemini API key for real calls

name: React Native skills
author: Callstack
description: Callstack's React Native skills in three bundles: building (performance, navigation, upgrades), testing (CI artifacts, device automation, exploratory QA) and migrating to RN. Drawn from a major RN consultancy's production work. Install with `npx skills add callstackincubator/agent-skills`.
use_case: Have the agent profile and fix a janky list screen in a React Native app using Callstack's performance skills.
safety_notes: Known RN consultancy; docs-only
works_with: Claude Code; Codex; Cursor; OpenCode; Gemini CLI

name: Awesome Agent Skills
author: VoltAgent
description: VoltAgent's collection of official skills from engineering teams plus community picks, compatible with most coding agents, and it says it avoids bulk AI-generated entries. One of the better-curated lists. Browse the README and install entries with their own commands.
use_case: Find an official skill from a vendor you already use, such as a database or payments company, before reaching for a community one.
safety_notes: A list; entries unvetted

name: NVIDIA skills
author: NVIDIA
description: NVIDIA's verified skills catalog for CUDA-X, robotics and simulation, RAG blueprints and platform tools, mirrored daily from product repos. Mainly for GPU and Physical AI work. Start with the nvidia-skill-finder skill via `npx skills add nvidia/skills`.
use_case: Ask the nvidia-skill-finder which skill to use for a CUDA or RAG blueprint task, then install only that one.
safety_notes: Official, but huge; some skills run vendor install scripts and set up SSH keys for clusters
works_with: Claude Code; Codex; Cursor; OpenCode; Gemini CLI

name: Agent Skills Discovery RFC
author: Cloudflare
description: A draft RFC for publishing Agent Skills at a /.well-known/ URL so agents can discover a site's skills, with an index, integrity checks and archive distribution. It is a spec, not a tool. Read it if you plan to publish skills for your own product.
use_case: If you publish skills for your own product, follow the RFC to serve them at a /.well-known/ URL agents can discover.
safety_notes: Spec text only

name: Awesome Claude Code
author: hesreallyhim
description: A hand-picked list of Claude Code resources: skills, agents, status lines, hooks, tooling and plugins, with an emphasis on quality and originality. Good for finding small useful tools like ccusage. Browse the README.
use_case: Find a status line, hook or small tool for Claude Code that someone has already built and reviewed.
safety_notes: A list; entries unvetted

name: Codex Skills Catalog
author: OpenAI
description: OpenAI's original Codex skills catalog, now marked deprecated in favor of the OpenAI Plugins repository. Still a readable set of examples for how Codex packages skills. For new work, follow OpenAI's Build plugins guide instead.
use_case: Read an example to see how Codex packages a skill, then build new ones as OpenAI plugins instead.
safety_notes: Official; a few skills install vendor CLIs from their official URLs. README: deprecated, use openai/plugins.

name: Ruflo (Claude Flow)
author: Reuven Cohen (ruvnet)
description: Ruflo is an agent meta-harness for Claude Code and Codex that adds swarms of agents, hooks, memory and an MCP server to a project via `npx ruflo@latest init`. Ambitious, with a very large surface. Read its hooks and postinstall before using.
use_case: Experiment with agent swarms on a throwaway repo after reading every hook and postinstall script it adds.
safety_notes: Its npm postinstall patches other packages in node_modules; very large hook surface

name: TDD Guard
author: Nizar Selander
description: TDD Guard uses Claude Code hooks to enforce test-driven development: it blocks writing implementation without a failing test and explains what to do instead. The author's newer Probity tool extends this to Codex and Copilot. Install with `/plugin marketplace add nizos/tdd-guard` and a test reporter.
use_case: Stop Claude Code from writing implementation code until a failing test exists for it.
safety_notes: Clean scan; hooks only check test state

name: Awesome Claude Skills (Composio)
author: Composio
description: Composio's list of 1000+ Claude skills and plugins for Claude, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and more, which also promotes Composio's MCP gateway. Use it to find skills, then vet each one. Browse the README.
use_case: Look for a skill idea, then install it from its original author's repo after vetting it.
safety_notes: Vendor-run list that also promotes Composio; vet each entry
related_note: Re-bundles copies of official Anthropic skills

name: Notion MCP Server
author: Notion
description: Notion's self-hosted MCP server; the README now says it is no longer actively maintained and recommends Notion's hosted Remote MCP instead. Kept here as reference. Use the remote server for new setups.
use_case: Only as reference: for new setups, connect Notion's hosted MCP so the agent can search and update your workspace.
safety_notes: Official; use a token scoped to the pages it needs
works_with: Claude Code; Codex; Cursor; OpenCode; Gemini CLI; Grok Bot / any MCP client
related_note: Unmaintained; Notion recommends its hosted MCP

name: Agentic Awesome Skills
author: sickn33 (Nick)
description: A library of nearly 3,000 SKILL.md playbooks for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and Gemini CLI, with 'AAS Core' to search the catalog and preview a plan before installing. The breadth is the selling point, but quality and provenance vary widely. Install with `npx agentic-awesome-skills --<agent>`; if you use it, copy single skills you have read.
use_case: Search the catalog for a niche skill and preview its plan, then copy just that skill after reading it line by line.
safety_notes: Huge unvetted bulk set incl. offensive pentest payloads; maintainer's GitHub bio carries a pump.fun token address
works_with: Claude Code; Codex; Cursor; OpenCode; Gemini CLI
ease_note: npx installer; must vet each skill

name: Amp Official Plugins
author: Amp
description: Official plugins and skills for Amp's agent mode, such as building scheduled runs. Amp is a closed-source agent CLI and IDE extension spun out of Sourcegraph, and it also loads `.claude/skills` natively. Install plugins from inside Amp.
use_case: In Amp, add the scheduled-runs plugin to have the agent run a maintenance task on a timer.
safety_notes: Official Amp org, but no LICENSE. Amp itself defaults to allow-all permissions when none are configured and allows MCP servers that match no rule (cited from search, not fetched directly); threads sync to ampcode.com; auto-updates are on

name: Claude for Financial Services
author: Anthropic
description: Claude Code plugins, skills and managed-agent cookbooks for finance work such as IC memos, earnings reviews and GL reconciliation, plus partner MCP connectors. It is for finance teams; install the plugins from the marketplace.
use_case: Have Claude draft an investment-committee memo from a company's filings using the financial-analysis plugin.
safety_notes: Official Anthropic; partner plugins connect to external financial-data MCP endpoints (LSEG, PitchBook, FactSet) and deploy scripts need ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. Scan otherwise clean

name: Continue
author: Continue
description: Continue is an open-source coding agent and assistant for VS Code and JetBrains with configurable models, rules and MCP tools. Its status changed in mid-2026, so treat it as a watch item. Install the extension from the marketplace.
use_case: Configure your own models, rules and MCP tools for in-editor chat and edits (watch its project status).
safety_notes: Large Apache-2.0 project, but its last commit (21 Jul 2026) says the login flow was retired after an acquisition; ownership and future are unclear. Don't adopt until that is clarified
install: Install the VS Code or JetBrains extension

name: Vibe Kanban
author: Bloop AI
description: Vibe Kanban lets you plan work as kanban issues, then start Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI or other agents in isolated workspaces per issue and review their diffs. The README now announces it is sunsetting. Run with `npx vibe-kanban`.
use_case: Create kanban cards for five small fixes and start an agent per card in isolated workspaces, reviewing each diff (note: it is sunsetting).
safety_notes: Clean scan, but the README says the project is sunsetting
works_with: Claude Code; Codex; Gemini CLI; OpenCode

name: Awesome Claude Skills (travisvn)
author: Travis VN
description: A curated list of Claude Skills with a clear explainer of how skills load (progressive disclosure) and pointers to official and community packs. Good orientation for newcomers. Browse the README.
use_case: Read the explainer on how skills load, then follow its links to the official packs.
safety_notes: A list; last updated Apr 2026

name: ClawHub community skills
author: OpenClaw
description: ClawHub is OpenClaw's public skill registry for publishing, versioning and searching SKILL.md packages and plugins. Security researchers found hundreds of malicious skills uploaded there. Don't install third-party skills from it.
use_case: None recommended: don't install third-party skills from it; use vendor marketplaces instead.
safety_notes: Snyk, Acronis and Palo Alto Unit 42 found hundreds of malicious skills uploaded there; don't install its third-party skills unreviewed
